results.title: Container-Optimized OS from Google documentation | Google Cloud Documentation
results.description: Container-Optimized OS is an operating system image for your Compute Engine VMs that is optimized for running Docker containers. With Container-Optimized OS, you can bring up your Docker containers on Google Cloud Platform quickly, efficiently, ...

results.title: Container-Optimized OS Overview | Google Cloud Documentation
results.description: Container-Optimized OS from Google is an operating system image for your Compute Engine VMs that is optimized for running containers. Container-Optimized OS is maintained by Google and based on the open source Chromium OS project.

results.title: Building Container-Optimized OS from source | Google Cloud Documentation
results.description: Container-Optimized OS is based on, and built using, tools from the open-source Chromium OS project.

results.title: Creating and configuring instances | Container-Optimized OS | Google Cloud Documentation
results.description: For simple scenarios where you want to run a single container on a VM or on each VM in a managed instance group, you can specify a container image and optional configuration parameters when you define the instance or instance template. Compute Engine creates the instance with the latest version of Container-Optimized OS and launches the specified container when the VM starts.

results.title: Container-Optimized OS release notes | Google Cloud Documentation
results.description: Note: Kubernetes version provided in the changelog corresponds to the Kubelet and the Kubectl version that are shipped in that Container-Optimized OS image.

results.title: Versioning scheme | Container-Optimized OS | Google Cloud Documentation
results.description: Major versions of Container-Optimized OS images are identified using what we call milestones. Container-Optimized OS milestones are monotonically increasing integers.

results.title: Using Arm-based Container-Optimized OS images | Google Cloud Documentation
results.description: Starting with Milestone 101, Container-Optimized OS publishes Arm-based OS images. The images can be used to create Tau T2A VMs on Compute Engine. To learn more about what types of workloads work well with Tau T2A, see Workload Recommendations.

results.title: Container-Optimized OS Release Notes: Milestone 81 | Google Cloud Documentation
results.description: Updated toolbox base container image to include security patches. ... Updated the built-in kubectl/kubelet to v1.17.6 to fix a bug that could result in the inability to start a cluster. Fixed a few OS Login CVEs: CVE-2020-8903, CVE-2020-8907, CVE-2020-8933.

results.title: Security Overview | Container-Optimized OS | Google Cloud Documentation
results.description: Container-Optimized OS enables several security-hardening kernel features, including Integrity Measurement Architecture (IMA), Audit, Kernel Page Table Isolation (KPTI), and some Linux Security Modules (LSMs) from Chromium OS.

results.description: Information about the Container-Optimized OS filesystem tree and how to mount disks.

results.title: Disks and file system overview | Container-Optimized OS | Google Cloud Documentation
results.description: This page provides an overview of the Container-Optimized OS file system and describes how to mount and format disks.

results.title: Automatic updates | Container-Optimized OS | Google Cloud Documentation
results.description: Container-Optimized OS uses an active-passive root partition scheme. The OS image is updated in its entirety, including the kernel, as opposed to package-by-package updates like on traditional Linux distributions.

results.title: Supported filesystems | Container-Optimized OS | Google Cloud Documentation
results.description: Container-Optimized OS comes with two built-in filesystems: EXT4 and XFS.
